articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Measurement inside the Car with Modern Embedded Wireless Technologies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The main goal of the paper is the measurement of electromagnetic field distribution inside the car with modern embedded wireless technologies. Measurement was performed in standard urban environment in the car with mobile phone Bluetooth connection for two cases, without usage of the phone and receiving the call. Results of the measurement show, that in modern car with more wireless technologies are many high frequency sources of electromagnetic fields. Although the values of these measured variables do not exceed the limit levels, it depends on the current state of the organism and the time of exposure.

articleTitle: The ferroresonance computation of single-phase small power transformers encountered in low-voltage electric installations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper quantitatively investigates the ferroresonance phenomena that occurs at the capacitive connection of a small power iron-core transformer that is encountered in low-voltage installations. The transients are often associated with high levels of distortion for the current and voltage waveforms that also exhibit extreme amplitudes. Thus, adopting an adequate analytical function for describing the transformer magnetic characteristics, the associated nonlinear differential equations that model the transient state, are numerically solved, extracting the main electric quantities temporal evolution. Additionally, their critical investigation is also performed suggesting some mitigations techniques of the phenomena undesirable consequences.

articleTitle: User presence monitoring based on Velostat pressure sensors and Arduino platform
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The presented article details a self-developed system for user presence monitoring either while lying in a bed or when sitting in a chair. Real-time information from the pressure sensor matrix is accessible via a website and customizable user-alerts are available. Apart from monitoring user presence, the system can also be used to gain insight into the anatomical well-being of the user - e.g. to detect scoliosis or other anatomical abnormalities. Planned future additions will include pre-fall detection based on user behavior analysis and extension of the pressure sensor network.

articleTitle: Detection of Arrhythmia in Real-time using ECG Signal Analysis and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: According to a study by the World Health Organization (WHO), cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of mortality across the world. Nearly 17.9 million deaths each year are due to CVDs, which equates to 31 % of all deaths worldwide. An estimated 85% of these deaths are caused by heart attack or stroke. Cardiac Arrhythmia is a major disorder humans' experience which can lead to fatal conditions such as Cardiac Arrest or Stroke. Unless it is tested by a physician, one cannot discern if he/she has Arrhythmia because of its asymptomatic nature in some cases. An Electrocardiogram (ECG) is commonly used to check a patient's heart rhythm. In this paper, our focus is to present a method through which Cardiac Arrhythmia can be detected and classified in real-time by a wearable ECG device. The MIT-BIH Database is used to train and evaluate our CNN model, resulting in an accuracy of 99.625%.

articleTitle: Guitar Segmentation in RGB Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this paper, we deal with the automatic segmentation of guitars that appear in RGB images towards a better understanding of multimedia concert contents. We apply Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) between two classes: guitar and non-guitar, to detect the image pixels belonging to guitar regions. In this work, we compare three semantic segmentation methods in the literature: DenseNet, DeeplabV3+ and HRNet based encoder-decoder networks. These networks are trained and tested with a manually annotated dataset created for this purpose, which addresses musical concerts and live scenarios. We measure the variance of the results against lack of examples, class unbalancing and noise. The results of this research indicate that HRNet-based networks perform better in guitar segmentation, showing robustness while reducing false positive and false negative rates.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulations of lightning protection photovoltaic modules
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This article describe procedure of modeling and simulations of lightning protection photovoltaic modules. To do this task has been chosen Ansys Electronic Desktop environment. At the beginning in article is present idea of investigations electric and magnetic field distribution between lightning protection system and PV modules. Then two modeling configurations are proposed: one with PV modules separated to LPS and the other with PV modules connected to LPS. The last configuration having a connection between photovoltaic system and LPS is practically used in case when the lightning separation distance cannot be achieved. Next are present results of simulations for various distances in each configuration. Finally conclusions based on obtained results are present.

articleTitle: Anomaly detection in ECG using wavelet transformation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper considers the wavelet transform in the analysis of electrocardiograms to detect the anomaly. Two types of anomalies have been considered: cardiac, and congestive heart failure. To solutions to this problem have been proposed. The first one applies the discrete wavelet transformation. Based on its results the diagnostic features are defined by applying a special set of statistical parameters of the transformed ECG signals. After the selection process, they are delivered as the input attributes to the set of different classifiers. In the second approach, the continuous wavelet transformation of ECG signals is applied, and the resulting two-dimensional image created in time-frequency space represents the input to the convolutional neural network. This network is responsible for the generation of features, and final classification at the same time. All calculations made in Python were performed on the publically available database Complex Physiologic Signals PhysioNet. The results of experiments have shown better quality measures (accuracy, sensitivity, and precision) when applying the discrete wavelet transform.

articleTitle: Passenger Exposure of Electromagnetic Field in the Train
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The modelling of passenger exposure of electromagnetic (EM) field by mobile phone in the train is presented in the paper with comparison of electric field strength values obtained by measurements in real situation inside moving train. Simulations were performed in cases where passengers were exposed to long-term radiofrequency field stemming from the use of mobile phones during railway transport. Dual band (900 and 1800MHz) PIFA antennas were designed and employed as radio frequency sources. Measurements of electric field strength were performed within a railway vehicle during ongoing mobile voice communication. The obtained levels of electric field strength did not exceed the limits for EM fields for human safety purposes.

articleTitle: Face Detection Using an Implementation Running in a Web Browser
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A face recognition system using machine learning has been developed. Node.js, Face-recognition.js, Dlib technology stacks were chosen to implement the system. The choice of means of realization of the client and server parts is carried out, the architecture of the application is defined. A desktop application has been created. An interface based on the HTML framework of the Twitter Bootstrap framework was developed and a comprehensive system testing was performed.

articleTitle: Fall Detection Using a Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Fall is one of the most common causes of injury. Falling is especially dangerous for the elderly people. Fortunately in recent years, there has been a growing popularity of smartphone devices, also among older people. Each such device is equipped with different sensors, including an accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer. The purpose of the article is to verify whether it is possible to effectively detect a fall from other daily physical activities. For the purposes of the research, linear and angular acceleration signals and magnetic field strength signals were recorded using a smartphone for various physical activities. An algorithm for extracting features based on energy calculated for wavelet details and approximation as well as entropy and Sevcick fractal dimension was proposed. The classification results obtained are good. The best results of classification accuracy were obtained for the gyroscope signal (average 96%). The precision was 0.88, the specificity −0.96 and the sensitivity −0.92. The proposed fall detection method was also verified on the UniMiB SHAR database, containing 7 types of activities registered for 30 people aged 18–60 (a total of 11771 examples of user activity).

articleTitle: Fryze Reactive Power in Electric Transport Systems with Stochastic Voltages and Currents
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the theoretical foundations of reactive power and additional power losses in a direct current electric transport system. Numerical calculations of inactive power and losses in the circuits of electric DC locomotives and trams have been carried out. Discrepancy between the sign of the instantaneous power and the presence of exchange processes in non-linear circuits of electric transport systems with stochastic voltages and currents is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Fractional Derivatives And Integrals Application with Caputo-Fabrizio Operator In Electromechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Using the Caputo-Fabrizio operator, the influence of substitution in the two-mass system linear model an integer derivatives on fractional derivatives is shown. Parameters changing of fractional PID controller in comparison with classical PID controller is analyzed. The influence on the system transient characteristics with the fractional order PID controller using is demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Calculation of Windings Differential Inductances of Electrical Devices in Mathematical Models with a Total Magnetic Flux
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The calculation of differential electromagnetic parameters (differential inductances and mutual inductances of windings) of electric machines and electromagnetic devices based on the mathematical models of their magnetic circuits with a total magnetic flux is proposed. These parameters are determined using the geometric dimensions and design features of the devices, the main magnetization curve of the magnetic core material and the winding currents.

articleTitle: Improved Mathematical Model for Analysis of Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Processes in Transformers
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: An improved mathematical model to analyze low-frequency electromagnetic processes in power transformers using MATLAB/Simulink software for visual modeling is developed. The model makes it possible to take into account electromagnetic connections between windings, their electromagnetic parameters and saturation of the magnetic circuit adequately.

articleTitle: Deep learning approach to the classification of selected fungi and bacteria
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Detection of microorganisms is of particular importance to human health and life, and for the industry in general. For this reason, we want this process to be as fast and precise as possible. We also expect that the automation of this activity (detection of microorganisms) can be widely used in various industries. This article is another attempt to the classification of microorganisms (a small group of selected species listed in ISO 17516:2014-11) that uses a deep learning approach with popular deep neural network (DNN) models. Before classification, the microorganisms were stained by two methods: Congo Red and the modified Gram stain. The classification results for the two staining methods are similar, but greater accuracy was obtained for Congo Red stain. The final results show that the popular DNN models (Xception, ResNet-50) perform well with this challenge and also show that it is not always beneficial to use the pre-trained weights of DNN models.

articleTitle: Multi-Person Re-Identification Based on Face, Pose and Texture Analysis in Unconstrained Videos
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: We present a method for re-identification of images of multiple people that appear in 2D RGB video sequences. The method needs no initialization or supervision and works with unconstrained sequences that include camera shot transitions and strong visual variations. In order to preserve tracking along the frames, our method combines facial recognition, clothing texture analysis and pose detection to compute a distance between tracked people at frame t-1, and detected people at frame t. We use techniques based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract this information from the people that appear in the images. The results obtained show that the proposed method achieves accurate tracking of the people even in those difficult sequences where faces appear occluded or people present similar textures.

articleTitle: Design of electromagnetic exposition system for irradiation of biological cultures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Design of an exposure system intended for irradiating biological cells with low frequency electromagnetic field in order to study impact of the electromagnetic field on the cells is reported in the paper. The purpose is to design the exposure system with high homogeneity of the magnetic flux density in a defined area of interest. Numerical simulations using CST Studio Suit are realized to adjust appropriate parameters of the system. The article presents how the input parameters influence the magnetic flux density distribution and its homogeneity. According to specified limitations appropriate design of the exposure system is reported and the results clearly show that the homogeneity reaches values of 99.97% in three of the five areas of interest.

articleTitle: Automatic Traffic Monitoring Using Images from Road Camera
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents an algorithm for visual inspection of traffic intensity. At first, the acquisition process of video material from a road camera is described. Then the algorithm for processing and analyzing images from the recorded video material is presented. Software was prepared in MATLAB environment. Algorithm tests were conducted in real conditions, at different times of the day, different atmospheric conditions and different levels of traffic intensity. Test results show that in good working conditions the vehicle counting accuracy was 95.6%. When the sun shined in the camera lens the counting accuracy decreased to 87.2%. The smallest accuracy 83.2% was noted for traffic jams.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Methods in Gene Recognition Problem
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to investigate and compare the performance of the set of methods used in selection of diagnostic features in classification problems. The investigated set includes such methods as Fisher criterion, reflefF, nearest component analysis, stepwise fit, Kolmogorov-Smirnov criteria, T2-test, Kruskall- Wallis test, feature correlation with class and SVM recursive feature elimination. The investigations compare their sensitivity to the class membership of data samples as well as the repeatability of the most important features. The selected set of the best features is used in selecting the most important genes and gene sequences stored in a dataset of gene expression microarray in prostate and ovarian cancers.

articleTitle: MCTS Based Agents for Multistage Single-Player Card Game
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents the use of Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithms for the card game Lord of the Rings. The main challenge was the complexity of the game mechanics, in which each round consists of 5 decision stages and 2 random stages. To test various decision-making algorithms, a game simulator has been implemented. The research covered an agent based on expert rules, using flat Monte-Carlo search, as well as complete MCTS-UCB. Moreover different playout strategies has been compared. As a result of experiments, an optimal (assuming a limited time) combination of algorithms were formulated. The developed MCTS based method have demonstrated a advantage over agent with expert knowledge.

articleTitle: Comparison of methods of recognition and classification of insulation defects of power equipment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the results of comparison of methods for recognition and classification of insulation defects from partial discharges depending on the number of extracted signal features. For this purpose, the built-in application MATLAB Classification Learner and Keras library were used. The results were compared using the learning algorithms Support Vector Machine, Nearest Neighbour Classifiers and Convolutional Neural Network for four types of partial discharge defects.

articleTitle: New effective algorithm for stabilizing periodic orbits of chaotic systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents a new algorithm for stabilizing periodic orbits, consisting of small changes in selected parameters of the chaotic system at any time of sampling. The system parameters are modified to minimize the distance of the trajectory trace from the fixed-point on the cross-section of the general Poincaré map. By modifying several parameters, it is possible to effectively eliminate chaotic oscillations in non-linear dynamic systems in the presence of strong interference and noise. The main attention has been focused on the Chua's circuit, which can be regarded as representative of a wide range of non-linear systems. The results of representative computer simulations were analyzed and interpreted in detail.

articleTitle: Particle-in-Cell code for gas discharge simulations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper describes a Particle-in-Cell code written in a modern programming language Julia. The code aims to simulate a process of electric discharge in gases. The most prominent features currently implemented: chemical reactions modeled with Monte Carlo collisions method, integration with a simple RLC circuit simulator and support for both XY and RZ coordinate systems. The capabilities of the software are presented by solving two classical problems: two-stream instability and RF discharge.

articleTitle: Automated System for Measuring the Temperature of the Desiccator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to create a modern automated complex for measuring the temperature of the desiccator using modern techniques and automation elements. Research on the automation methods of the desiccator is conducted. An automated complex for measuring the temperature of the desiccator is created. A functional diagram of the thermocouple interface device with an analog-to-digital converter is developed. A low-pass filter is synthesized for noise filtering. Results of experimental studies of the automated complex with low-pass filter are provided. The introduction of integrated automation tools in the grain processing industry can significantly reduce costs and increase the output of finished products, as well as increase productivity and improve working conditions.

articleTitle: Combining texture analysis and deep learning in renal tumour classification task
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Current advances in Computer Vision allowed solving the vast majority of tasks in this field. However, the analysis of medical imaging still requires specialized algorithms, usually employing a lot of expert knowledge. This research aims to create an automated computer system able to differentiate 8 types of renal cancer types. Such a system can contribute to earlier diagnosis and better prioritization of patients waiting for medical consultation. The multi-feature ensemble system integrates 2 distinct groups of feature generation and classification: texture analysis and deep learning. In the first approach, three independent methods of feature generation: GLCM, SFTA, and Unser algorithm have been used. Their results are then passed to the SVM classifier. The second group utilizes transfer learning applied to pretrained deep models, developed within the ILSVR challenge. Combining both individual approaches with weighted voting yields results reaching 93.6 % of weighted F1-score evaluated in 10-fold cross validation mode.

articleTitle: The use of non-linear acoustic analysis to objectively evaluate the voice of people with Parkinson's disease
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Voice acoustic analysis in people with Parkinson's disease can be a valuable and objective tool supporting the diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases. The article analyses the application of non-linear coefficients for the parametrization of the speech signal representing the vowel “a” with prolonged phonation in patients with Parkinson's disease. The study was conducted using three different non-linear techniques for the generation of speech signal features. The research utilized recordings conducted at the Department of Neurology at the Medical University of Warsaw. The discriminatory ability of individual coefficients was evaluated using the LDA technique and k-nn method. The recognition accuracy is about 85 %.

articleTitle: Design of Truly Distributed Storage for Large Medical Datasets
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the architecture design of the unique IT system that combines the advantages of DLT (blockchain) and DHT (peer2peer) technologies for the storage of large medical files, such as MRI scans or genetic data. Medical data is characterized by exceptional confidentiality and at the same time need for fast and reliable access when saving a patient's health or life. Modern tools of cryptography allow us to achieve these effects using a distributed system architecture, which has the additional advantage of being independent of one data controller.

articleTitle: Evaluation of EMF inside Motorcycle Helmet with installed Bluetooth Communicator under Laboratory Condition
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Evaluation of electromagnetic field (EMF) inside motorcycle helmet with Bluetooth communicator is the main goal of the paper. Measurement was made under the laboratory condition using two helmets with integrated Bluetooth communicator set in intercom mode for three cases, helmet distance set to 500mm without communication, same distance with communication and for distance of 2500mm with ongoing communication. As measurement setup BK PRECISION 2650A spectral analyser together with Rohde & Schwarz antennas were used.

articleTitle: The Method of Student Testing in Electrical Engineering in On-line Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Mathematical models, methods and algorithms used in the control of student knowledge and adaptive control of distance network-centric learning processes in the field of electrical engineering are proposed and researched. The means and methods of knowledge control are analyzed and the prospects of using adaptive methods based on student models and educational material are substantiated, as they are the most objective and effective. Based on the analysis of basic problems, mathematical models of pedagogical testing, which are used in the design of such systems, are proposed and considered. It is proposed to use an adaptive model with a combination of models on fuzzy mathematics for effective control of student knowledge. An algorithm of adaptive testing has been developed, which allows more flexible and accurate assessment of student knowledge.

articleTitle: Design of a device for simultaneous measurement of heart sounds and electrical activity of the heart for educational purposes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the design and construction of a heart sound and ECG measuring device. The practical part also deals with the creation of a graphical user interface in MATLAB programming environment used for communication and control of the device. The user interface is designed for analysis of measured data.

articleTitle: Design of Halbach Ring Flux Reversal Machine: A Finite Element Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A Halbach Ring Flux Reversal Machine (FRM) has been designed using Finite Element (FE) analysis and simulation results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Baking of Thin Electrically Non-conductive Layers by Indirect Induction Heating
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A model of baking electrically non-conductive thin layers (paints, lacquers and other covering material) is presented. The process of baking, whose purpose is to protect the metal substrate from unfavourable influences of environmental medium, is realized by indirect induction heating of the metal substrate that transfers heat to the thin layer by conduction. The electromagnetic and temperature fields in the system are described by two partial differential equations for the magnetic vector potential and temperature. Some important results of the process are verified experimentally with a very good accordance.

articleTitle: Voltage THD suppression by autonomous power source - case study
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The object of study is autonomous power source composed of combustion engine driving synchronous generator of 25 kVA. The voltage THD of this system was about 7%, exceeding the threshold of 5% acceptable by the customer. Dominant in the THD was the third harmonic (150 Hz). Replacement of the source with semiconductors' inverter was out of the question for the customer. On the other side space for suppression elements was limited. In the first approach serial line inductance and passive LC filters were tried but without success. Theoretically they are without any effect in idle mode. The only possible way seemed to be application of separation Delta/Star transformer. Measurements with mounted separation transformer confirmed convenience of the choice.

articleTitle: Investigation of Artificial Cracks by Sweep Frequency Eddy Current Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article deals with the utilization of the sweep frequency eddy current technique as an alternative method for material crack evaluation. The new eddy current probe is designed and presented. Experimental measurements are carried out to evaluate resolution of the probe while the harmonic signal is used for the excitation. The gained results are presented and discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: A Real-time AC E-Motor Model for An Open-link Locomotion Module
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A real-time model of AC electric motor drive for an open link locomotion module is investigated. A new numeric single-step method of average voltage in the integration step is used for the modelling of the electrical drive integrated in the locomotion model. The features of this method are the high operation performance and numerical stability. It is shown that proposed approach significantly decreases computational time, hence allowing for taking into account agile dynamics of the locomotion module when synthesizing observers or controllers.

articleTitle: Comparison of Chosen Electric and Magnetic Field Parameters Influence on Biological Samples Using Numerical Modelling and Simulation Methods
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This article focuses on use of numerical simulation methods as a suitable tool for calculation and comparison of specific electromagnetic quantities within the irradiated volume. Comparison of two different applicators presented herein was performed to confirm homogeneity of low frequency magnetic field used in real experiments conducted on yeast cell cultures. Moreover, simulation results also provide valuable insight into the evaluation of electric field parameters, focusing especially on conductive current density, which could potentially affect transmembrane electric currents at cellular levels, or induce undesirable heating within the irradiated volume as well.

articleTitle: Use of asynchronous electric motors in naval electric propulsion systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the propulsion losses, the types of powers and forces acting on a ship, the components of the total conversion efficiency and the energy required for a ship propulsion. An important part of the paper is the presentation of the naval power plant simulation program-the electric propulsion engine. In order to perform an energy analysis, the propulsion system is calculated separately both according to the ship's load and according to the propeller-driven electric motor. Thus, the variation of the existing factors in the statics and dynamics of the ship, the variation of forces and efficiencies, must be considered. Also, the power characteristics, loading load, speed and propeller transmission - all responsible for energy consumption, must be considered. The insertion of electronic power devices into propulsion drive systems generates voltage and harmonic distortions in the ship's electrical network.

articleTitle: An Approximation to Gaussian Wavelet Suitable for Analog Filter Implementations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fourth order approximation function to 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> Gaussian wavelet using time domain analysis of linear time-invariant (LTI) systems and the conditions for the transfer functions of realizable analog filters. Fourth order approximation is used for compact circuit implementations which might use a cascade of only two biquads. Transfer function for a realizable filter and the related Simulink model are also supplied in the paper with numerical results.

articleTitle: Classification of High - Voltage Ignition Waveforms Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A detailed analysis of secondary voltage waveforms displayed by an oscilloscope is commonly acknowledged as a key to diagnosing automobile ignition systems as well as some mechanical components of spark - ignited combustion engines. Many ignition systems troubles may be identified by experienced service technicians due to an assessment of some characteristic parts of a high-voltage waveform: the dwell time, firing line, burn time and oscillations. However, the analysis of many data collected over a long period, if done manually, can be awkward and time-consuming. The focus of the article is an application of a deep learning method for the detection and classification of selected parts of highvoltage waveforms generated by an ignition coil. The study concluded that an application of the ADAM optimization algorithm for deep learning can help develop a model for highvoltage signal segmentation which yields the average classification accuracy greater than 99%.

articleTitle: Patch-based renal CTA image segmentation with U-Net
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This article presents an innovative processing method of computed tomography image-slices for automatic identification of kidneys and cancers boundaries. The system was developed based on the use of U-Net convolutional neural network. The innovative solution proposed in the presented experiments uses the technique of automatically partitioning the input data into frames of fixed dimensions, containing only areas of interest. The developed technique allows obtaining accurate boundaries of the kidneys and cancers with high accuracy, comparable to a human expert. The obtained segmentation accuracy is satisfactory and equals 96 % for renal, 74% for renal cell cancers and 90 % for cystics.

articleTitle: Bioamplifier using active electrodes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The specialized bioamplifier for active electrode applications is presented in this paper. Our device presents 4 channeled bioamplifier with option to connect 3 couples of active electrodes and one couple of standard electrodes. The measured signal processing and digitalization are based on the ADS1194 chip by Texas Instruments. The graphical user interface is also presented in this article. The end of the article is focused on the measurement of electrocardiogram and electromyogram to prove the ability of the prototype to measure bioelectrical signals. The article also shows the simple design of active electrode for capacitive coupled sensing with integrated ultralow input bias current operational amplifier LMP7721 in configuration as voltage buffer.

articleTitle: Multi-Patch Blending improves lung cancer growth pattern segmentation in whole-slide images
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this study, we introduce a technique to generate synthetic histologic image data by blending parts of different images into a new image patch. The proposed approach, which we call multi-patch blending (MPB), crops parts of two histologic images of tumor growth patterns annotated with single but different labels and pastes them into a newly created image patch comprising areas with two different annotations. A Cycle-GAN model is employed in MPB to smooth out transitions between the pasted image crops and make the output image patch look realistic. The goal of implementing the MPB is to support the task of semantic segmentation of lung adenocarcinoma grown patterns in whole-slide images (WSI). We used MPB to increase the number of training patches extracted from a set of 18 WSIs with sparse annotations. De facto, MPB was implemented as a novel data augmentation strategy. U-Net trained with MPB-generated patches achieved 13% higher F1-score than the U-Net trained with original (sparsely annotated) patches in a 4-class semantic segmentation task.

articleTitle: Biometric System of Access to Information Resources
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The biometric system of access to information resources has been developed. The software and hardware complex are designed to protect information resources and personal data from unauthorized access using the principle of user authentication by fingerprints. In the developed complex, the traditional input of login and password was replaced by applying a finger to the fingerprint scanner. The system automatically recognizes the fingerprint and provides access to the information resource, provides encryption of personal data and automation of the authorization process on the web resource. The web application was implemented using the Bootstrap framework, the 000webhost web server, the phpMyAdmin database server, the PHP scripting language, the HTML hypertext markup language, along with cascading style sheets and embedded scripts (JavaScript), which created a full-fledged web-site and Google Chrome extension with the ability to integrate it into other systems. The structural schematic diagram was performed. The design of the device is offered. The algorithm of the program operation and the program of the device operation in the C language are developed.

articleTitle: Definition of Models of Elements in Linear Periodically Time-Varying Circuits in Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article proposes a way to reduce the cost of computer time needed to form a mathematical model of the linear periodically time-varying circuit in the form of a symbolic system of linear algebraic equations, which is formed by L.A. Zadeh's equation and the frequency symbolic method for the frequency domain. The concept of a time-varying matrix model of conductivity of the individual elements of a circuit was introduced in the form of some matrix. On the basis of such models the system of linear algebraic equations of the linear periodically time-varying circuit is formed much faster and by usual rules, for example, as by the rules of a method of nodal voltages for the circles with constant parameters. The results of computer experiments are given. The considered a time-varying matrix models are convenient to use while designing the radio engineering devices that are modeled by the linear periodically time-varying circuits, and, in particular, the devices of noise-tolerant covert special purpose radio engineering systems.

articleTitle: Deep learning approach to creating bone models
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 21st International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper discusses the usefulness of deep neural networks in tasks of automatic segmentation of bone structures from CT data. Three different neural network models (PSPNet, U-net and Segnet) were trained to perform the segmentation task. Pixels in the CT image are assigned to 3 following classes: background, patient outline and bones. The mean and classwise Intersection over Union (IoU) measure was evaluated for each network outcome. The most exact segmentation results were obtained with the use of U-net model, with mean IoU value equal to 93.2%.
